title: Closed self-enrichment and change of enriching base
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the monoidal categorical-algebra convention of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be closed symmetric monoidal infinity categories, and write $[X,Y]_{\mathcal C}$ and $[X,Y]_{\mathcal D}$ for the right adjoints to tensoring by $X$. Let $L:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal C:R$ be an adjunction with $L$ strong symmetric monoidal; thus $L\mathbf1\simeq\mathbf1$ and $L(X\otimes Y)\simeq LX\otimes LY$ coherently. An adjunction means natural equivalences of the full mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(X,RB)$.

For every small set $O$ and family $(A_o)_{o\in O}$ in $\mathcal C$, there is a categorical algebra on the discrete object set $O$ enriched in $\mathcal C$, with hom objects $[A_o,A_{o'}]_{\mathcal C}$. Its composition is adjoint to iterated evaluation and its units are adjoint to identities, including all associative and unital coherences. The right adjoint $R$ has the adjoint lax symmetric monoidal structure. Applying it to the hom objects, units and compositions yields a categorical algebra enriched in $\mathcal D$, with hom objects $R[A_o,A_{o'}]_{\mathcal C}$, naturally in the family and its restrictions. Neither categorical algebra is asserted complete when $O$ is discrete.

There are natural equivalences
$$R[LX,B]_{\mathcal C}\simeq[X,RB]_{\mathcal D}.$$
They identify evaluation and currying, including their parameter simplices and composition coherences. In particular $R[\mathbf1,B]_{\mathcal C}\simeq RB$. All these assertions hold in any larger universe containing the displayed objects.

source.place: Corollaries 7.4.9--7.4.10 for self-enrichment from a closed action; section 5.7 for change of enriching category. The adjoint lax structure and mixed internal-Hom comparison are the agent-formulated coherent adjunction specialization; no completeness assertion is taken from the unproved expectation in Remark 7.4.8.
